assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column separate from actual credit score column
assertions.evidence: Table columns are: Scenario | age | creditScore | hasStableIncome | Result?. No dedicated 'Credit threshold' column.

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms not abstract codes
assertions.evidence: Values: 700, 651, 650, 500, APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING_REVIEW, true, false

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes
assertions.evidence: Scenarios start with outcomes: 'Approved — above threshold', 'Rejected — below threshold', 'Pending — income not provided'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language, not code identifiers
assertions.evidence: Columns include code identifiers: 'creditScore' (should be 'Credit score'), 'hasStableIncome' (should be 'Stable income?')

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with ?
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Test method has @DisplayName or descriptive method name
If @Description longer than one line, uses text block (triple quotes) not concatenation
Multiple tables address distinct concerns, not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: standardApplicantDecision and seniorApplicantDecision

assertions.text: Each table has only rows needed to express its rules, no unnecessary permutations
assertions.evidence: Standard table: 8 rows; Senior table: 7 rows testing specific boundaries without exhaustive permutations

assertions.text: Age boundary, credit score categorization, and income status separated into distinct methods
assertions.evidence: Credit score and income are tested together within each age-based method; no distinct method for credit categorization or income status
